paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the people who look like they're winning aren't the ones to copy. The teacher says, "Do not envy wicked men or desire their company," and he gives his reason: "the evil man has no future; the lamp of the wicked will be extinguished" (Proverbs 24:1, 20). So when somebody's shortcuts start looking shiny, remember that I once stared at a cookie on the cooling rack for ten minutes before it was even done, and that one wasn't ready either.

Wisdom is the thing worth wanting. The teacher says a house is built by wisdom, and through knowledge its rooms are filled with "every precious and beautiful treasure" (Proverbs 24:3-4). He says wisdom is sweet to your soul, and that if you find it, "there is a future for you, and your hope will never be cut off" (Proverbs 24:14). Even when you fall, the righteous man "still gets up" (Proverbs 24:16), so a stumble doesn't end the story, and that is GREAT news for a stamper who tips over reaching for the top oven rack.

Wisdom also changes how you treat people. The teacher says to rescue those being led away to death, and he reminds us that He who weighs hearts knows (Proverbs 24:11-12). He says not to gloat when your enemy falls, because the LORD sees it (Proverbs 24:17-18). So fear the LORD, keep good counsel close, and let your wanting go to the right place. That's advice worth keeping right where you can reach it.
